Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and the players of West Indies are waiting patiently near the boundary ropes before taking the field. From the visuals, it looks like there is a fair bit of dew already, which will favor the batters for sure. It will be the duo of Saif Hassan and Tanzid Hasan to start the innings for Bangladesh. Akeal Hosein will take the new ball for West Indies as he generally does.
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, 166 is what Bangladesh need to win and take the crucial 1-0 lead in this series. They are a team in form but the target is a bit more than what we usually see at this venue. West Indies will be eyeing up early wickets as no one knows how much effect the dew will have in this run chase. All in all, it should be a cracker, so stay tuned for the chase.

The man of the moment, Rovman Powell is down for a quick chat. He says that it is important for him to give inspiration to the other guys, being the most senior player. Add that the last few months haven't been great for them. Mentions that it is not an easy track to bat on, and the message to the bowlers will be to control the Powerplay. Reckons it is a good score if they do well in the first six overs, but if not, they might be just 10 runs short as 175 would have been ideal.

Bangladesh will be a tad disappointed as they seemed in control of the innings for much of the 20 overs but having played just 5 bowlers took its toll in the end. Nasum Ahmed started things in a very tidy manner and so did Taskin Ahmed but he was taken to the cleaners in his 2nd over. Rishad Hossain did get a wicket but was very expensive as Taskin came back strongly to pick up two wickets. Mustafizur Rahman showed good consistency but Tanzim Hasan Sakib got hit for plenty in the final over, costing a huge momentum shift in this game.

After electing to bat first, West Indies couldn't get off the blocks quickly in the Powerplay but they did well not to lose any wickets either. However, just when Alick Athanaze started to fire, he got out and Brandon King had to keep anchoring from one end. Skipper Shai Hope looked in pristine touch but King struggled for timing and got out soon after the drinks break. Having lost two wickets in two balls, West Indies needed a rebuild and that's exactly what they got. Rovman Powell used all his experience to hang around and chanced his arm at the death and both he and Hope finished with unbeaten scores in the 40s.

Carnage in the end from Rovman Powell in what is his 100th T20I for West Indies and together with skipper Shai Hope, he has taken the visitors to a solid total. The Windies' innings was simmering all throughout but in the end, they will be pretty pleased about the score on the board.

A couple of runs to end the innings then! Tanzim Hasan Sakib goes fuller and on off, Rovman Powell drills it wide of long off for a couple of runs. The throw comes in at the batter's end, but as Powell is running back, he unknowingly blocks the vision of Litton Das, who fails to collect the throw. However, the batters do not run on the overthrow. Good spirit shown by the Windies. West Indies finish on 165/3!

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now! The fans have come in numbers for this game in Chattogram, and there is a buzz around the stadium. We can see the Bangladesh players spread out and take their respective field positions. Alick Athanaze and Brandon King are the two openers for West Indies. Litton Das is going with spin straightaway, as he has handed over the new ball to Nasum Ahmed. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Farveez Mahroof is pitchside. He says that conditions are quite muggy but perfect for cricket. Adds that the pitch is much lighter than the one in Mirpur and there are cracks on this track, but they aren't shaky. Reckons that the ball will come onto the bat much better and feels that even though the recent average score here batting first has been 148, it is a 160-plus wicket.

We are moments away from the start of the first T20I, but before that, the players from both sides walk out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. The players first observe a minute's silence following the passing away of Barishal Division physio, Hasan Mahmud, who was just 47 years old. On to the anthems then, it will be West Indies' first, followed by the national anthem of Bangladesh.

Litton Das, the skipper of Bangladesh says that he is definitely fully fit. Adds that he didn't do much training in the last few weeks because with that type of injury, you cannot train much, but he is feeling good. Adds that they have played a lot of cricket here in BPL and do not mind batting second on this wicket. Ends by saying that they are playing with three seamers, two spinners, and six batters.

Shai Hope, the captain of West Indies, says that they will bat first because it looks a bit dry to begin with and want to get the best batting conditions. Adds that they need to put the ODI series behind them and start afresh against a strong Bangladesh side. Reckons that it is important to start with a win here and feels that the surface does look on the drier side, and they'll have to wait and see if it stays that way.
Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Saif Hassan, Litton Das (C/WK), Tawhid Hridoy, Shamim Hossain, Nurul Hasan, Rishad Hossain, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Nasum Ahmed, Tanzim Hasan Sakib.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Alick Athanaze, Shai Hope (C)/WK), Roston Chase, Sherfane Rutherford, Rovman Powell, Jason Holder, Romario Shepherd, Akeal Hosein, Khary Pierre, Jayden Seales.

Teams winning the toss often prefer to bowl first, anticipating the pitch to get slower.
